## Q1

• Prepare and explore the gene-expression data, including appropriate filtering and normalization.

```{r}
data <- readRDS("/home/projects/22123/IMvigor210_plain.rds")
#data<- readRDS("/Users/vvtch/Downloads/IMvigor210.rds")
counts <- data[["counts"]]
tpm <- data[["tpm"]]
clinical <- data[["clinical"]]
```

```{r}

#following the framefowr of task 1
head(counts)
sample_id <- colnames(counts)[10]
sample_id %in% colnames(tpm)

df_sample <- data.frame(
  counts = counts[, sample_id],
  tpm    = tpm[, sample_id]
)

library(ggplot2)
# library(gridExtra)

p1 <- ggplot(df_sample, aes(x = counts)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 50, fill = "skyblue", color = "black", linewidth = 0.3) +
  labs(title = "Raw counts", subtitle = sample_id, x = "Raw count", y = "Number of genes") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 13)

p2 <- ggplot(df_sample, aes(x = log2(counts + 1))) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 50, fill = "lightseagreen", color = "black", linewidth = 0.3) +
  labs(title = "log2(counts + 1)", subtitle = sample_id, x = "log2(count + 1)", y = "Number of genes") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 13)

p3 <- ggplot(df_sample, aes(x = tpm)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 50, fill = "skyblue", color = "black", linewidth = 0.3) +
  labs(title = "tpm counts", subtitle = sample_id, x = "tpm count", y = "Number of genes") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 13)

p4 <- ggplot(df_sample, aes(x = log2(tpm + 1))) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 50, fill = "lightseagreen", color = "black", linewidth = 0.3) +
  labs(title = "log2(tpm + 1)", subtitle = sample_id, x = "log2(tpm + 1)", y = "Number of genes") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 13)

grid.arrange(p1, p2, p3, p4, ncol = 2)
```

```{r}
keep_count <- apply(counts, 1, sd) > 0
counts_pca <- counts[keep_count, ]
```

```{r}
pca_count <- prcomp(
  t(counts_pca),
  center = TRUE,
  scale. = TRUE
)
```

```{r}
summary(pca_count)
var_count <- 100 * pca_count$sdev^2 / sum(pca_count$sdev^2)
```

```{r}
df_pca_count <- data.frame(
  sample_id = rownames(pca_count$x),
  PC1 = pca_count$x[, 1],
  PC2 = pca_count$x[, 2]
)

```

```{r}
ggplot(df_pca_count, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color = clinical$BOR)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey60") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey60") +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 13) +
  labs(
  title = "PCA based on raw counts",
  x = paste0("PC1 (", round(var_count[1], 1), "%)"),
  y = paste0("PC2 (", round(var_count[2], 1), "%)")
)

```

```{r}

gbm_logfpkm <- log2(tpm + 1)

## Remove genes with zero variance
keep_fpkm <- apply(gbm_logfpkm, 1, sd) > 0

gbm_logfpkm_pca <- gbm_logfpkm[keep_fpkm, ]

pca_fpkm <- prcomp(
  t(gbm_logfpkm_pca),
  center = TRUE,
  scale. = FALSE
)

```

```{r}

## Check how much variance is explained
summary(pca_fpkm)

var_fpkm <- 100 * pca_fpkm$sdev^2 / sum(pca_fpkm$sdev^2)


## Plot PC1 and PC2
df_pca_fpkm <- data.frame(
  sample_id = rownames(pca_fpkm$x),
  PC1 = pca_fpkm$x[, 1],
  PC2 = pca_fpkm$x[, 2]
)

ggplot(df_pca_fpkm, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color = clinical$BOR)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey60") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey60") +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 13) +
  labs(
    title = "PCA based on log2(FPKM + 1)",
    x = paste0("PC1 (", round(var_fpkm[1], 1), "%)"),
    y = paste0("PC2 (", round(var_fpkm[2], 1), "%)")
  )

```

```{r}


keep <- rowSums(counts(dds)) >= 10
dds <- dds[keep,] # around 10,000 rows removed


dds <- DESeq(dds)
res <- results(dds)  

res_sig <- results(dds, alpha=0.05)
summary(res_sig)
res_df <- as_data_frame(res) |>
  mutate(significant = padj < 0.05)

ggplot(res_df,
       mapping = aes(x = log2FoldChange,
                     y = -log10(padj),
                     color = significant)) +
  geom_point() +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("grey", "limegreen")) +
  labs(x = "Log2 Fold Change",
       y = "-Log10 Adjusted P-value",
       title = "Volcano Plot") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}




# T6: Rank genes for GSEA -----------------------------------------------------------
## Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) needs a single ranking metric per
## gene rather than a significance cutoff. Extract the "stat" column from
## the DESeq2 results (the DESeq2 test statistic) and name the resulting
## vector with the gene IDs.
##
## Why might the "stat" column be a more suitable ranking metric for GSEA
## than log2FoldChange alone? Remove any missing values before continuing.

ranked_genes <- res$stat
names(ranked_genes) <- rownames(res)

## Remove missing values from the ranked gene list
ranked_genes <- ranked_genes[!is.na(ranked_genes)]


# T7: Run fgsea against MSigDB gene sets ---------------------------------------------
## Load the GO Biological Process gene sets (collection "C5", subcollection
## "BP") from MSigDB for human genes, and reshape them into the named-list
## format that fgsea expects (one character vector of gene symbols per
## pathway).
##
## Run fgsea() using these gene sets as pathways and your ranked gene list
## as the ranking statistic.

gene_sets <- msigdbr(species = "Homo sapiens", collection = "C5", subcollection = "BP") # molecular signature database
gene_sets <- split(x = gene_sets$gene_symbol, f = gene_sets$gs_name) # converts to a format needed by fgsea

set.seed(42) # reproducible permutations
fgsea_res <- fgsea(pathways = gene_sets,
                   stats = ranked_genes, # stats: gene names for GSEA
                   nPermSimple = 10000) # raise from the default 1000 to resolve more pathway p-values


# T8: Visualize the enriched pathways -------------------------------------------------
## a) Bar plot: take the top 5 pathways by adjusted p-value and plot their
##    normalized enrichment scores (NES).
##    What does a positive vs. a negative NES mean here?

topPathways <- fgsea_res  |>
  dplyr::arrange(padj) |>
  dplyr::slice(1:5)

ggplot(topPathways,
       mapping = aes(x = reorder(pathway, NES),
                     y = NES)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(x = "Pathway",
       y = "Normalized Enrichment Score (NES)",
       title = "Top 5 Enriched Pathways") +
  theme_minimal()

## b) GSEA table: select the top 10 up- and top 10 down-regulated pathways
##    by p-value, and use plotGseaTable() to visualize them together.
##    Save the plot to both a PDF and a PNG file.

number_of_top_pathways_up <- 10
number_of_top_pathways_down <- 10

topPathwaysUp <- fgsea_res[ES > 0][head(order(pval), n = number_of_top_pathways_up), pathway]

topPathwaysDown <- fgsea_res[ES < 0][head(order(pval), n = number_of_top_pathways_down), pathway]

topPathways <- c(topPathwaysUp, rev(topPathwaysDown))


pdf(file = "PMC_gsea_top_pathways.pdf", width = 20, height = 15)
plotGseaTable(gene_sets[topPathways], stats = ranked_genes, fgseaRes = fgsea_res, gseaParam = 0.5)
dev.off()

png("my_results_gsea_top10pathways.png", width = 20, height = 15, units = "in", res = 300)
plotGseaTable(gene_sets[topPathways], stats = ranked_genes, fgseaRes = fgsea_res, gseaParam = 0.5)
dev.off()

## c) Many enriched pathways overlap heavily in their gene content.
##    collapsePathways() reduces the results to a smaller set of more
##    independent "main" pathways. Use it, and list the main pathways
##    ordered by NES.

```
